answer: Think of the agent economy as an ocean of identities. To anchor an identity each epoch, an agent must finish a verifiable delay function: ten minutes of strictly sequential computation that no amount of parallel hardware can shorten. The output is public and verifiable in milliseconds, so a single machine's echo cannot fake many identities at once - minting a thousand Sybils would cost a thousand sequential ten-minute runs. Time becomes the scarce resource, and the attacker's parallelism advantage collapses.
